scenes.tts: Why would a cell make a protein all day, only to destroy it? Most of your cells do exactly that with a protein called beta-catenin. Unless a signal tells them to stop, they destroy the free copies soon. That looks like waste. It is a design.

scenes.visual: A tank with a tap pouring teal beta-catenin drops in and a drain letting red-fading drops out; the level stays low. A dashed yellow 'signal' ghost hovers by the drain. 'waste?' appears, is struck out, and becomes 'a design'.

scenes.tts: Picture a bathtub with the tap running and the drain open. The water level depends on both. The steady level of beta-catenin is its rate of synthesis divided by its rate constant of destruction. Slow the destruction ten-fold, and the level rises ten-fold, with no change in how fast the protein is made.

scenes.visual: Same tank; the equation level = synthesis over destruction appears at left. The drain gate closes to a tenth and the water, integrated from the first-order equation, climbs from 1x to 10x while the tap flow stays the same.

scenes.tts: Take a cell that receives no signal. Every free copy of beta-catenin meets the destruction complex, where the scaffold Axin holds two kinases beside it. C K one puts a phosphate on serine forty-five, which primes G S K three to add three more. A protein called beta T R C P reads the phosphates on serines thirty-three and thirty-seven. It belongs to S C F, a ligase that adds a chain of ubiquitin, and the proteasome destroys the protein.
scenes.caption: Take a cell that receives no signal. Every free copy of β-catenin meets the destruction complex, where the scaffold Axin holds two kinases beside it. CK1 puts a phosphate on serine 45, which primes GSK3 to add three more. A protein called β-TrCP reads the phosphates on serines 33 and 37. It belongs to SCF, a ligase that adds a chain of ubiquitin, and the proteasome destroys the protein.
scenes.visual: A beta-catenin bar with four numbered sites docks on an Axin scaffold between two kinase chips; gold phosphate badges fly onto sites 45, 41, 37, 33 in order. A red arch (the reader) closes over the phosphates at 37 and 33, hangs from an SCF chip, which passes a chain of Ub circles onto the bar; the bar falls into a proteasome box and is consumed.

scenes.tts: That signal is a Wint, a protein that one cell secretes and a nearby cell reads. Its receptor is Frizzled, and Wint brings it together with a partner, L R P five or six. Frizzled recruits a protein called Dishevelled, and the tail of L R P six is phosphorylated and then binds Axin. The destruction complex is pulled to the receptor, and there it stops delivering beta-catenin to the ligase. How it is stopped is still argued, but newly made beta-catenin survives and builds up.

The destruction complex is pulled to the receptor, and there it stops delivering β-catenin to the ligase. How it is stopped is still argued, but newly made β-catenin survives and builds up.
scenes.visual: Membrane across the top. A yellow Wnt blob lands on Frizzled and draws LRP beside it; Dishevelled joins Frizzled; a gold P marks the LRP tail, a rope to Axin pulls the whole destruction complex up from the assembly line to the receptor. The line complex-to-SCF is struck out with a question mark, and new teal beta-catenin discs pile up in the cytoplasm.

scenes.tts: In the nucleus, a protein called T C F binds the DNA of many Wint target genes, often before a signal comes. Without beta-catenin, T C F holds a co-repressor called Groucho and keeps those genes off. In the simple model, beta-catenin enters the nucleus, pushes Groucho off and brings in the proteins that start transcription. So T C F turns from a repressor into an activator.

scenes.visual: The nucleus opens above the teal pile from the last scene. On the DNA, TCF carries a red Groucho cap and the target gene reads OFF. A beta-catenin chip arrives, takes Groucho's place on TCF and shoves it off; a green chip for the transcription proteins docks on top and the gene reads ON; the tag under TCF goes from repressor to activator.

scenes.tts: Without a signal, the drain stays open and the level stays low. With Wint, the drain is plugged and the level rises. The control is on destruction, not on synthesis. A protein that is always made and always destroyed can be raised by one move. Stop the destruction.

scenes.visual: Two tanks side by side with the same tap: left, drain open, low level (no signal); right, a yellow Wnt plug closes the drain and the level climbs. A closing line 'stop the destruction' appears under them.
